answer: Bonded collateral escrows make each identity’s stake slashable, while asymmetric capital depreciation raises the cost of repeated faults. When cedar, river, and quartz—or any k coordinated identities—equivocate in correlated ways, pairwise evidence yields O(k²) penalty exposure. Detection can also apply an exponential multiplier to aggregate capital loss as linked claims are depreciated, so splitting control across a sybil swarm increases rather than dilutes risk.
